column2: The cooks complain that my ward [From.GetFirstName] haunts the kitchens day and night. [From.GetSheHeCap] steals pies from the windowsills, begs sweetmeats from the pantry maids and was found this morning asleep in the larder, smeared to the ears in honey.
A growing child needs to eat!
Fetch the birch.
Explain to [From.GetHerHim] the virtue of moderation.
I will pray to the gods for [From.GetHerHim].

At the feasts my ward [From.GetFirstName] eats sparingly and drinks only water, while the rest of the court gorges itself. When a servant offered [From.GetHerHim] a second helping of venison, [From.GetSheHe] shook [From.GetHerHis] head and said that one was enough for anybody.
Moderation is a fine virtue.
Let the gluttons of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] good sense.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must learn to enjoy life!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] has started to hoard. Coins, buttons, a silver spoon from the high table, the toys of the other children: anything that glitters disappears into a box under [From.GetHerHis] bed, and [From.GetSheHe] counts it every night.
Wealth is power. Let [From.GetHerHim] learn its worth.
Fetch the birch.
[From.GetSheHeCap] needs a lecture on charity.
The gods punish the greedy. I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].

My ward [From.GetFirstName] gave [From.GetHerHis] cloak to a beggar at the gates today, and came home shivering. Yesterday it was [From.GetHerHis] supper, and the day before, [From.GetHerHis] new boots.
A generous heart is a noble thing.
Let the misers of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] kindness.
Charity is for naive weaklings!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] will not stir from [From.GetHerHis] bed before noon. [From.GetSheHeCap] dozes through [From.GetHerHis] lessons, leaves [From.GetHerHis] chores to the servants and is found asleep in the hay loft whenever [From.GetSheHe] is wanted.
Let [From.GetHerHim] rest. [From.GetSheHeCap] will be busy enough when [From.GetSheHe] is grown.
Fetch the birch.
[From.GetSheHeCap] needs a lecture on diligence.
I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].

My ward [From.GetFirstName] is always the first at [From.GetHerHis] lessons and the last to leave. [From.GetSheHeCap] copies [From.GetHerHis] letters until the candle burns out and asks the steward to teach [From.GetHerHim] the accounts.
Good. Hard work will make [From.GetHerHim] great.
Let the idlers of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] diligence.
The child needs to lighten up!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] cannot bear to see anyone else with something [From.GetSheHe] does not have. When another child got a new wooden sword, [From.GetFirstName] sulked for a week, and then the sword turned up broken in the well.
Envy makes one strive for more.
I will beat some respect into [From.GetHerHim].
Explain to [From.GetHerHim] that envy poisons the heart.
The gods despise the envious. I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].

My ward [From.GetFirstName] nursed a fallen fledgling back to health this spring, and now [From.GetSheHe] has taken in a lame dog from the kennels. The servants say [From.GetSheHe] has never spoken an unkind word to any of them.
A kind heart is a fine thing.
Let the brutes of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] kindness.
Kindness is weakness. The world will eat [From.GetHerHim] alive.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] flew into a rage again today. [From.GetSheHeCap] lost at a game of knucklebones and threw the bones, the board and finally a stool at the other children, screaming until [From.GetSheHe] was hoarse.
A fiery temper makes a fierce warrior.
I will beat some respect into [From.GetHerHim].
Teach [From.GetHerHim] to master [From.GetHerHis] temper.
I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].

My ward [From.GetFirstName] spent the whole afternoon untangling a knotted fishing net that the other children had given up on. [From.GetSheHeCap] did not complain once, and when it was done, [From.GetSheHe] simply smiled.
Patience is the mark of a wise ruler.
Let the hotheads of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] patience.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is too meek. A ruler must act!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] has started to give orders to the servants as if [From.GetSheHe] owned the castle. [From.GetSheHeCap] will not sit below the salt, will not play with the children of the household knights and corrects [From.GetHerHis] tutors when they mispronounce [From.GetHerHis] titles.
[From.GetSheHeCap] knows [From.GetHerHis] worth. Good.
I will beat some respect into [From.GetHerHim].
Remind [From.GetHerHim] that pride comes before a fall.
I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].
My ward [From.GetFirstName] would rather eat with the stable hands than at the high table. When the steward bowed to [From.GetHerHim], [From.GetSheHe] blushed and bowed back.
Humility is a rare virtue among the highborn.
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] humility.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must remember who [From.GetSheHe] is!
My ward [From.GetFirstName] lied to me again. [From.GetSheHeCap] swore on [From.GetHerHis] mother's name that the stable boy had let the horses loose, but the stable boy was with me all morning.
A clever tongue will serve [From.GetHerHim] well at court.
I will beat some respect into [From.GetHerHim].
Teach [From.GetHerHim] the value of honesty.
I will pray for [From.GetHerHim].

My ward [From.GetFirstName] spends hours in the shrine every day. [From.GetSheHeCap] knows the prayers by heart, scolds the servants for blasphemy and has asked me twice whether [From.GetSheHe] may join the priesthood when [From.GetSheHe] is grown.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] spends hours at prayer in the shrine of the Sun every day. [From.GetSheHeCap] fasts on the holy days without being told, recites the scriptures by heart and scolds the servants when they forget their devotions.
The gods have touched [From.GetHerHim]. Good.
Too much piety makes a poor ruler.
My ward [From.GetFirstName] broke a precious vase this morning. Nobody saw it happen, and [From.GetSheHe] could easily have blamed a servant, but [From.GetSheHe] came straight to me and confessed.
Honesty is a noble virtue.
Let the liars of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
Sometimes it is wiser to keep quiet...
Only fools tell the truth!
My ward [From.GetFirstName] ran from a goose today. A goose. The other children have made up a song about it, and now [From.GetSheHe] will not leave [From.GetHerHis] room.
Caution has kept many a lord alive.
There is no shame in a quiet life.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must learn to face [From.GetHerHis] fears!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] climbed the highest tower of the castle today to fetch a falcon that had escaped its mews. The whole court held its breath, but [From.GetSheHe] came down with the bird on [From.GetHerHis] wrist, grinning from ear to ear.
Courage is the first virtue of a warrior.
Let the cowards of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
Bravery and foolishness are not the same thing.
My ward [From.GetFirstName] hides behind the tapestries whenever guests arrive. When a visiting lord spoke to [From.GetHerHim] at dinner, [From.GetSheHe] turned red, stammered and ran from the hall.
Still waters run deep. Leave [From.GetHerHim] be.
Fetch the birch.
Talk to [From.GetHerHim] gently.
I will pray to the gods to give [From.GetHerHim] strength.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] knows everyone in the castle by name, from the steward to the scullery maids. [From.GetSheHeCap] is always at the heart of every game and every song, and the guests adore [From.GetHerHim].
A ruler must be able to win hearts.
Let the dour folk of this court learn from [From.GetHerHim]!
I thank the gods for [From.GetHerHis] warmth.
[From.GetSheHeCap] talks too much and thinks too little.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] told me today that [From.GetSheHe] will be a king one day, or an emperor, and that everyone who laughed at [From.GetHerHim] will kneel. [From.GetSheHeCap] did not seem to be joking.
Aim high, child. Aim high.
Be content with what the gods have given you.
My ward [From.GetFirstName] wants nothing and asks for nothing. While the other children squabble over toys and titles, [From.GetSheHe] sits in the sun and seems perfectly happy.
A contented heart is a happy one.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must want more from life!

My ward [From.GetFirstName] was asked to settle a quarrel between two pages today. [From.GetSheHeCap] heard neither of them out and simply sided with the one who had given [From.GetHerHim] an apple that morning.
A ruler's word is law. Let [From.GetHerHim] learn that.
Teach [From.GetHerHim] to judge fairly.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] was asked to settle a quarrel between two pages today. [From.GetSheHeCap] listened patiently to both of them, asked the servants who had seen it, and judged against [From.GetHerHis] own favourite.
Justice is the foundation of every realm.
A ruler need not be bound by such scruples.
My ward [From.GetFirstName] asked the priest today why the gods let children starve if they are so mighty. The priest had no answer, and now [From.GetSheHe] laughs during the prayers.
A sharp mind questions everything.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must learn to fear the gods!
The kennel master came to me today, white with anger. My ward [From.GetFirstName] has been tormenting the hounds, and this morning [From.GetSheHe] was found pulling the wings off a sparrow, laughing.
A ruler must be feared.
I will beat some respect into [From.GetHerHim].
Teach [From.GetHerHim] that cruelty shames a noble.
I will pray for [From.GetHerHis] soul.

[Root.Liege.GetTitledName] has children who are growing up without a guardian to teach them. [guardian_offered_child.GetFirstName] is of an age to learn the ways of the world, and who better to teach [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] than a loyal vassal? It would be a great honour, and a ward close to the liege's heart is a valuable thing.
I will offer to raise [guardian_offered_child.GetFirstName].
I have enough to do as it is.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] will decide.

My liege,

I have watched your child [guardian_offered_child.GetFirstName] grow, and it would be my honour to take [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] into my household and raise [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] as my ward. I would teach [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] everything I know, and guard [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] as if [guardian_offered_child.GetSheHe] were my own.

Your faithful servant,
[From.GetTitledName]
Gladly. Take good care of [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim].
No. The child stays with me.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will be glad.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will be disappointed.
The child will be told.

My loyal vassal,

I accept your offer with thanks. [guardian_offered_child.GetFirstName] will come to your household before the month is out. Raise [guardian_offered_child.GetHerHim] well.

[From.GetTitledName]
I will not fail you, my liege.

My vassal,

I thank you for your offer, but my child will be raised under my own roof.

[From.GetTitledName]
As my liege wishes...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has told me that I am to go and live with [ward_guardian.GetTitledName], who will be my guardian from now on and will teach me everything a [Root.GetLordLady] must know.
I hope [ward_guardian.GetSheHe] is kind.

My guardian [ward_guardian.GetTitledFirstName] does not pray the way we pray at home. [ward_guardian.GetSheHeCap] follows [ward_guardian.Religion.GetName], and [ward_guardian.GetHerHis] shrine is full of strange images and candles. I am curious.
I will ask [ward_guardian.GetHerHim] about [ward_guardian.GetHerHis] gods.
I would rather go and play with my friends.
[ward_guardian.GetTitledFirstName] will answer.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] came to me today with a hundred questions about [Root.Religion.GetName]: who the gods are, why we pray to them, and why [From.GetSheHe] was taught differently at home. The child is clearly eager to learn.
I will teach [From.GetHerHim] the true faith.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will work it out on [From.GetHerHis] own.
[From.GetFirstName] may take your faith.

My guardian [From.GetTitledFirstName] has told me all about [From.Religion.GetName], and the more I hear, the more it makes sense. The gods of my guardian are mighty, and they answer those who pray to them.
From now on I will follow [From.Religion.GetName].

I have lived in the household of my guardian [ward_guardian.GetTitledFirstName] for so long now that I speak like [ward_guardian.GetHerHis] people, eat like them and sing their songs. When I think of home, it seems a long way away.
I am one of them now.
I would rather go and play with my friends.

My ward [From.GetFirstName] has taken to our ways as if [From.GetSheHe] had been born among us. [From.GetSheHeCap] speaks with our accent, knows our songs and our customs, and the household treats [From.GetHerHim] as one of their own.
What a bright child!

My [From.GetSonDaughter] [From.GetFirstName] is slow to talk. Other children of [From.GetHerHis] age chatter all day, but [From.GetSheHe] points, tugs at sleeves and swallows half of every word. The nursemaids whisper about it when they think I cannot hear.
Speak slowly with [From.GetHerHim] and set an example.
The birch will bring the words out.
Let [From.GetHerHim] take [From.GetHerHis] time.
Send [From.GetHerHim] to the nursemaids. They have more patience.
[From.GetFirstName] climbed onto my knee tonight, looked me in the eye and asked where children come from. The servants have gone very quiet.
I will tell you when you are older.
Well, there are bees, you see, and flowers...
Be quiet or I will slap you!

[From.GetFirstName] will not sleep without a candle. [From.GetSheHeCap] swears there are goblins under the bed and daemons in the corners, and screams the keep awake whenever the light goes out. In this world, [From.GetSheHe] is not entirely wrong.
Mock [From.GetHerHim] until [From.GetSheHe] is ashamed of it.
Sit with [From.GetHerHim] and find out what [From.GetSheHe] fears.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must face the dark alone.
[From.GetFirstName] has been fighting again. This time [From.GetSheHe] left the steward's boy with a bloody nose and came home grinning. The other parents are starting to complain.
Good. [From.GetSheHeCap] won.
Put that energy into lessons and drills instead.
[From.GetSheHeCap] needs discipline.
Let the priests pray the anger out of [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetFirstName] has a chest full of wooden soldiers, a hobby horse, a painted ball and three dolls, and still [From.GetSheHe] wails that [From.GetSheHe] has nothing to play with.
Let [From.GetHerHim] have more toys.
Go and play outside!
Teach [From.GetHerHim] some humility.
Off to the nursemaids with you, leech!
[From.GetFirstName] asked me today why the other children have mothers and [From.GetSheHe] does not. I did not know what to say.
Your mother is with the gods now, and watches over you.
Your mother has gone on a long journey.
Do not ask me things like that!
[From.GetFirstName] has no friends. The other children run off when [From.GetSheHe] comes near, and [From.GetSheHe] spends the days alone on the walls watching them play.
Friends are overvalued anyway.
Help [From.GetHerHim] along.
Give [From.GetHerHim] toys to win friends with.
[From.GetFirstName] begs to skip lessons today and play 'Who is afraid of the Black Knight' with the other children instead.
You may play after your lessons.
Play all you like, then.
You can play with the birch! Go to your lessons!
[From.GetFirstName] asked me what heathens are, and whether they have horns.
Heathens are people just like us, only they pray to other gods.
They are servants of the Ruinous Powers, spawned from the Realm of Chaos!
They are people like us, but they are our enemies.
[From.GetFirstName] and the other children have taken to climbing the outer walls and fencing with sharpened sticks. One of the stable boys already broke an arm.
Let them play. What harm can it do?
Set a few limits on the games.
A curfew!
[From.GetFirstName] came to me with a serious little face and asked whether [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] is real.
Of course, my child. Now go and play.
Certainly. Let me tell you all about the gods.
My child, let me explain how things really are...
A servant died last night, and [From.GetFirstName] wants to know why people die.
Because they are careless.
Everyone dies, sooner or later.
It is all part of the gods' plan.
[From.GetFirstName] asked me whether [From.GetSheHe] will rule one day.
Of course you will.
If you deserve it, you shall.
No, you will not, silly child!
[From.GetFirstName] has found the joys of the feast hall: wine, music and dancing until dawn, with the older courtiers cheering [From.GetHerHim] on. [From.GetSheHeCap] is far too young for it.
There is nothing I can do.
Curfews!
[From.GetFirstName] wants to know why we fight people who pray to the same gods as we do.
Fighting for faith is a game for priests.
I fight whoever I like!
Sometimes even your brother can be your enemy.
[From.GetFirstName] wants to know why the temples are full of gold while the peasants outside them starve.
The gods reward the poor in the next life.
Why not share some of your own, then?
[From.GetFirstName] saw me let a poacher go with a warning, and wants to know why.
He needed the deer more than I did.
A good deed a day keeps a lord content.
[From.GetFirstName] informed a peasant today that he was [From.GetHerHis] property, and ordered him to carry [From.GetHerHim] across the courtyard. The man did it.
That is right, child.
That is it, you are under curfew!
[From.GetFirstName] asked me whether a tree that falls in the woods makes a noise if no one is there to hear it.
A good question. Think on it yourself.
Think about something useful instead.
[From.GetFirstName] says that since we will all die anyway, there is no point in fussing about life, and asks why [From.GetSheHe] should not simply enjoy it.
I suppose you are right.
And what about enjoyment?
[From.GetFirstName] wants to know how [From.GetSheHe] can best serve [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
Be brave against the enemies of the faith!
Be just to all the faithful.
I caught [From.GetFirstName] in the yard again with an old practice blade from the armoury, drilling when [From.GetSheHe] should be at [From.GetHerHis] needlework.
Let her do it.
Back to the needle with you.
The other children call [From.GetFirstName] a coward. [From.GetSheHeCap] came to me in tears again today.
I will teach you to fight myself.
Speak up for [From.GetHerHim] before the court.
Do not worry about them.
[From.GetFirstName] crept down into the dungeons and came back up with a bloody knife the gaolers left lying about. [From.GetSheHeCap] is fascinated by it.
I will teach [From.GetHerHim] some useful skills.
Tell [From.GetHerHim] it is all a game.
Take the knife and teach [From.GetHerHim] mercy.
I found [From.GetFirstName] curled up in a chair behind the biggest book in the library, when [From.GetSheHe] should have been at [From.GetHerHis] chores.
Take pride in your learning.
Make a joke of it.
Get [From.GetHerHim] out among the other children.
[From.GetFirstName] is plain, and knows it. [From.GetSheHeCap] watches the fair courtiers with longing and asks whether [From.GetSheHe] will ever look like them.
You will never be as good looking as them.
You look fine to me.
[From.GetFirstName] hears every day how fair [From.GetSheHe] is, and is starting to believe it is all that matters.
Show it off. Beauty is a weapon.
Looks fade. Learn something.
At the market [From.GetFirstName] haggled a merchant into the ground over a bag of sweetmeats, then counted the change three times. [From.GetSheHeCap] counts money whenever [From.GetSheHe] can.
Teach [From.GetHerHim] the joys of money.
Teach [From.GetHerHim] the joys of giving.
Money belongs to the gods.
[From.GetFirstName] cannot keep away from the visitors at court, and pesters every envoy and merchant with questions about where they come from.
Introduce [From.GetHerHim] to them.
Tell [From.GetHerHim] to stop it!
[From.GetFirstName] practises with a sword at every chance, often against the old soldiers, who laugh as [From.GetSheHe] charges at them.
This will make [From.GetHerHim] a great knight!
Make sure [From.GetSheHe] does not hurt [From.GetHerselfHimself].
This will make [From.GetHerHim] a great swordmaster!
I walked in on [From.GetFirstName] and another child kissing behind the stables. Both turned the colour of beetroot.
Teach [From.GetHerHim] the ways of courtly love.
Lecture [From.GetHerHim] on virtue and vice.
[From.GetFirstName] spends all [From.GetHerHis] days in the kitchen, eating whatever the cooks put in front of [From.GetHerHim]. The drill yard has not seen [From.GetHerHim] in weeks.
Drag [From.GetHerHim] to the drill yard.
Not my concern. Let [From.GetHerHim] eat until [From.GetSheHe] bursts!
[From.GetFirstName] climbed the highest tower of [Root.Location.GetName], on the outside, and waved at me through the window at the top.
Curiosity never killed anyone!
Teach [From.GetHerHim] a lesson [From.GetSheHe] will not forget.
Strictly forbid it.
[From.GetFirstName] is sick: feverish, pale and too weak to leave bed. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks me to make it stop.
Make [From.GetHerHim] fast to atone for [From.GetHerHis] sins.
Pay a physician.
Only the gods decide over life and death.
[From.GetFirstName] has confided that [From.GetSheHe] feels drawn to [From.GetHerHis] own sex, and has stopped hiding it.
Make [From.GetHerHim] fast to atone.
Beat it out of [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetSheHeCap] will grow out of it.
[From.GetFirstName] makes friends with ease, twisting the truth to whatever shape each new friend wants to hear.
The goal justifies the means.
Your tongue will get you into trouble!
[From.GetFirstName], a child of my court, has no guardian. No one teaches [From.GetHerHim] letters, arms or manners, and [From.GetSheHe] runs wild through the halls.
I will raise [From.GetHerHim] myself.
Leave [From.GetHerHim] be. The halls will raise [From.GetHerHim].
A ward of mine complained and called my court inferior, at least in comparison to the child's father's court.
To be a ward in [Root.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName]'s court is improving my stature. I had no idea how different a [Root.Father.GetTitle]'s court and a [Root.Guardian.GetTitle]'s court could be!
My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] told me how much [From.GetSheHe] enjoyed being in the court of [From.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] and how [From.GetHerHis] stature had improved!

My child was lured into stealing cookies and smearing jam all over the kitchen by one of my wards! The cook gave them a hearty scolding and then sent them to me, both still smeared with jam and covered in cookie crumbs.

I have seen the looks on my wife [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName]'s face every time she looks at my ward. The longing on her face tells me she wants to have children of her own, and I'll gladly help her with that.

My ward [From.GetTitledFirstName] came running for me, tears streaming down [From.GetHerHis] face and snot creeping towards [From.GetHerHis] mouth.\n"[Root.GetFirstName], please help me! The other children are not nice to me!"

A foreign court can teach a child all kinds of important lessons, everything from respecting to understanding and even adapting to other people's traditions and culture. My ward has learnt several important lessons of life in my court, foreign as it may be to the father's court.

I knew I had made a good decision when I sent my child to [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s court. The life lessons learnt from a foreign court are worth its weight in gold and my child has learnt to respect and understand other people's traditions and culture.

No matter how many questions I ask, [Root.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] always has an answer and is ever so patient with me! Our relationship has grown and I feel as if I have formed a strong mentor-relationship with [Root.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName].
My ward [From.GetFirstName] is inquisitive and asks so many questions it is hard to answer them all. I try my best and for every answer I give, [From.GetFirstName] seems to like me even more.
Try to improve your court to impress the child
What else can I learn?
I'm proud of you, [From.GetFirstName]!
Punish the fosterling, forgive my child
Shall we try some more?
Why should I care?
The father will be pleased
Good, good
This will be good to me
I think we have become friends!
For a simple [Root.GetTitle], my court is nothing to be ashamed of!
You will both clean the stables for a whole week!
You will grow strong from that
I can handle things on my own
Have the child sweep the stables
I forgive you, but promise me this won't happen again!
I'll punish [child_bully.GetFirstName], don't you worry
Birch the child
Punish my own child for being so impressionable!
s child [Root.GetFirstName] is thriving under [Root.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName]'s care
s child is thriving under [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s care
has formed a strong relationship with [This.GetHerHis] ward [Root.GetTitledFirstName]
